summary: CSV ingest line-delimiter + charset mismatch causing embedding ID shift and rerank top-k inversion
description:
Issue summary: After a CSV upload via the Console ingest flow, the customer sees frequent rerank quality regressions and intermittent 5xxs. Impact: ~12% of search queries return inverted top-k (relevant doc falls out of top 10) and ~4% of rerank requests return 500/502 when embedding dims are detected as mismatched. Environment: LexisSearch production account (enterprise tenant), ingest via Console CSV upload from EU office that uses Latin-1 default encoding. Steps to reproduce:
1) Upload sample CSV with CRLF line endings and ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) encoded file via Console -> Ingests -> CSV import.
2) Trigger a rerank API call on the newly ingested dataset (route: /v1/rerank with reranker-v1).
3) Observe rerank scores and API responses.
Observed behavior: Some CSV rows are parsed with an extra leading invisible character (0xA0 / non-breaking space) in the first field, which causes the ingest preprocessor to treat that row as a new batch boundary. This shifts the mapping between embedding vectors and document IDs for a subset of the batch. The embeddings-service detects a dimension mismatch (expected 768, got 769 after an accidental padding conversion) and triggers a CPU fallback path, causing elevated latency and occasional 500s when the fallback queue is saturated. Expected behavior: Console should normalize charset to UTF-8 and strip leading invisible chars so row-to-id mapping remains stable. Embedding dim should remain consistent and fallback should not be triggered unless model actually emits different dims.
Initial hypothesis: Latin-1 encoded CSV + CRLF combined with a trim-sanitizer that only runs on UTF-8 input caused an extra non-printable insertion during ingestion. Batching logic uses a row delimiter heuristic that is charset-sensitive, resulting in off-by-one index alignment between doc metadata and embedding vector batch.
Relevant logs (redacted):
[2026-03-09T18:02:13Z] ingest-csv: file_open: charset=ISO-8859-1, line_ending=CRLF, rows=12, columns=6
[2026-03-09T18:02:13Z] preprocess: normalize_line_endings -> applied: false (file not flagged as UTF8)
[2026-03-09T18:02:14Z] batcher: grouping rows -> batch_size=8 -> boundary_indexes=[0,4,8,12]
[2026-03-09T18:02:15Z] embed-service: accept_vectors -> expected_dim=768, received_dim=769 -> queue_fallback=triggered
[2026-03-09T18:02:20Z] reranker: request_id=abc123 -> status=500 -> error="embedding-dim-mismatch"

investigation_notes:
Findings summary:
- Root trigger: Console CSV importer did not force UTF-8 decoding. When ISO-8859-1 files contained non-breaking spaces (0xA0) or high-bit characters, the preprocessor that strips whitespace failed to recognize them, leaving invisible bytes at field boundaries.
- Side effect: Batcher heuristic that detects row boundaries for multiplexing relied on a sanitized delimiter index; the invisible bytes changed tokenization length heuristics causing an off-by-one alignment between metadata array and embeddings array.
- Embedding pipeline: The embedder runtime applied a conversion step that, when encountering certain byte patterns, appended a padding byte (0x00) to align vector proto. This caused a single-vector dim mismatch (769) which triggers CPU fallback and sometimes overflow in fallback queue -> 500/502s.
- Mitigation proof-of-concept: Forcing UTF-8 decode + NFKC normalization at ingest eliminates the garbage byte and prevents batch misalignment.
- Risk areas: Existing datasets already ingested with Latin-1 remain misaligned in vector-store; re-ingest is required to correct mapping. There is risk of similar issues for other one-off encodings (Windows-1252).
- Links: Slack thread #support-lexissearch, runbook: confluence/pages/INGEST-CHARSET-NORM, debug PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/499 (draft).
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation: Forced UTF-8 decode and NFKC normalization in Console ingest pipeline rolled out to us-west-2 on 2026-03-12 (hotfix). This reduced new-uploads regressions by ~87%.
Permanent plan: Engineering will ship a hardened sanitizer that: (1) detects file charset and coerces to UTF-8, (2) normalizes line endings and invisible whitespace, (3) validates row-to-vector counts before committing batch, and (4) rejects uploads with mixed encoding with a clear customer-facing error recommending re-save as UTF-8. Target for permanent fix: 2026-03-20.
Customer remediation: Offer LexisSearch one-time bulk re-ingest using a migration tool that re-decodes historical CSVs to UTF-8 and re-submits to embeddings pipeline in a safe dry-run mode. Also providing credits for rerun.
Follow-ups: Create an automated audit to scan existing vector-store for dim outliers and mismatched metadata counts. Add an alert to detect embed-service CPU fallback rate > 0.5% in a 5m window.
